title.narrative: Emergency response to flooding in Juradó, Choco

description.narrative: Since mid-June, the municipality of Juradó in the department of Chocó in Colombia has been affected by heavy rains, high tides and gales that have caused flash floods and overflowing of the Juradó, Partadó and Jampabadó rivers, causing at least 7,535 people (2,417 families) to be affected by the partial and/or total loss of their homes, crops, livestock, farmyard animals, goods, merchandise, food, school and institutional infrastructure seriously damaged, and premises destroyed, creating a humanitarian emergency in the entire territory. Of the families affected, 750 are indigenous communities of Emberá Dóbida de Jumaracarrá, Teresita Ancestral, Buenavista, La Victoria, Punto Caimito, Dos Bocas, Pichinde, Cedral, El Bongo, Eyasake and Patato, a large part of the houses of the indigenous community of Pichindé were submerged by the waters of the Jampabadó river. In addition, 1,667 families are Afro-descendants, 12 communities are doubly affected by flooding and confinement due to armed actions and clashes between non-state armed groups, and 1 community is displaced in the municipal capital. The project will be a rapid emergency response providing food and hygiene kits to 393 households, with a co-financing from SNPS/Caritas Colombia (290 food kits and 293 hygiene kits with CAFOD funding).
